instruction: Select all images containing a clock.

game.semantic_variant: Select all things made to tell the time.
game.hint: Select all that apply. If you are unsure, use your best judgement.
game.explanation: Ordinary clocks count, and so do the clock whose hands are human arms and the grandfather clock with a cuckoo bursting out of it: impossible, but still clocks. The phone hung on the wall showing a clock face and the sundial are borderline cases, recorded without a verdict. The mirror, the decorative plate and the compass are not clocks.

correct: Clocks identified. Your time has been well spent.
Correct. The Department will be on time for once.
partial: Partially correct. A clock is still unaccounted for.
Partially correct. Some clocks ran out of time.
incorrect: Incorrect. The Department has stopped the clock.
Incorrect. Time has been wasted, and recorded.

selection_review.reason: Version 2 of C08, adding the re-rendered clock with human arms as hands and the cuckoo bursting from a grandfather clock. Nine distinct, standardised images reviewed together at tile size: two ordinary clocks (round wall clock with a mint-green rim; lime-green twin-bell alarm clock), two impossible clocks (generated wall clock whose hands are small human arms; generated grandfather clock with a living cuckoo bursting out in a spray of splinters), two borderline timekeepers (generated smartphone hung on a wall showing an analogue dial; photographed bronze sundial on a pedestal) and three round, dial-like non-members (wall mirror, painted plate, compass). Views, colours and settings vary within each role. The running alarm clock, the hourglass clock and the longcase clock photograph remain in the collection.
